title: OneDrive and SharePoint: block screen capture of sensitivity-labelled PDFs in the web viewer
summary: Hold: the label-permissions path skips Edit label and the wizard choices needed to reach Access control. The roadmap facts and documented permissions are supported; searches did not locate a default or a separate switch for the planned PDF viewer restriction.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; Risk assessment; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The roadmap plans screen capture blocking in the OneDrive and SharePoint web PDF viewer in Edge for PDFs whose sensitivity label lacks Copy (EXTRACT); unlabelled PDFs and labels granting Copy are outside its description.
claims.quote: The OneDrive and SharePoint web PDF viewer will block screen capture in Microsoft Edge when users open PDFs whose sensitivity (MIP) label without Copy (EXTRACT) permission.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note
claims.claim: The Copy usage right is encoded as EXTRACT and appears as Copy (EXTRACT) in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Common name: Copy Encoding in policy: EXTRACT ... Name in the Microsoft Purview portal: Copy (EXTRACT)

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Granting Copy enables copying data, including screen captures.
claims.quote: Enables options to copy data (including screen captures) from the item into the same or another item.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Rights Management can prevent captures by many commonly used Windows screen capture tools when Copy is not granted.
claims.quote: By not granting the Copy usage right, Rights Management can prevent screen captures from many of the commonly used screen capture tools on Windows platforms.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure and Change & support
claims.claim: The Rights Management page says browsers other than Edge cannot prevent screen captures, including browser use of Office for the web; browser-dependent capture behaviour is therefore a concern.
claims.quote: In addition, browsers other than Edge can't prevent screen captures. Browser use includes Outlook on the web and Office for the web.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The SharePoint and OneDrive label documentation separately says screen captures are not prevented for encrypted documents in Office for the web.
claims.quote: For encrypted documents in Office for the web, screen captures aren't prevented.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Screen capture prevention does not prevent other ways of sharing displayed information, such as a camera or retyping.
claims.quote: For example, a user intent on sharing displayed information can take a picture of it using their camera phone, retype the data, or simply verbally relay it to somebody.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: One sensitivity label can grant different permissions to different users.
claims.quote: Note that the same label can grant different permissions to different users.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: In some applications, Copy also allows the entire document to be saved unencrypted.
claims.quote: In some applications, this right also allows the entire document to be saved unencrypted.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first row
claims.claim: The printed route goes directly from selecting a sensitivity label to Access control and its permission settings.
claims.quote: To edit an existing label, select it, and then select the Edit label icon. ... This action starts the Edit sensitivity label configuration, which lets you change all the label settings.
claims.fix: Replace the path with 'Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > label > Edit label > Define the scope for this label > Files & other data assets > Choose protection settings for the types of items you selected > Control access > Access control > Configure access control settings > Assign permissions now > Assign permissions > Choose permissions'. The entry and Edit label step are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels; the scope and Control access choices are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/encryption-sensitivity-labels. Keep both sources, which the briefing already cites.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first row
claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <label> -EncryptionRightsDefinitions <Identity1:Rights1,Rights2> modifies a label's granted usage rights.
claims.quote: The EncryptionRightsDefinitions parameter specifies the rights users have when accessing protected. This parameter uses the syntax Identity1:Rights1,Rights2;Identity2:Rights3,Rights4.

claims.where: controls[0].note
claims.claim: EncryptionRightsDefinitions is meaningful with EncryptionEnabled set and EncryptionProtectionType set to Template.
claims.quote: This parameter is meaningful only when the EncryptionEnabled parameter value is either $true or $false and the EncryptionProtectionType parameter value is Template.

claims.where: Governance controls; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Set-Label is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell and requires assigned permissions there.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell. ... To use this cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell, you need to be assigned permissions.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second row; Scope
claims.claim: PDF label support can be enabled in the Purview portal under Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > Protect PDFs with Auto-labeling.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Policies > Auto-labeling policies ... if you see a message Protect PDFs with Auto-labeling, select this banner

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second row; Scope
claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableSensitivityLabelforPDF $true enables PDF label support at tenant level.
claims.quote: Sets properties on the SharePoint Online organization. ... [-EnableSensitivityLabelForPDF <Boolean>]
